what_it_does: Quantum computers store information in quantum bits (qubits), but physical qubits on a chip can only interact with their immediate neighbors — two qubits that are far apart on the chip cannot perform an operation directly. To run an algorithm, a compiler must insert extra swap operations that physically move qubit information around until the right qubits are adjacent; this is called the qubit routing problem. Too many swaps make the circuit so deep (so many sequential steps) that errors accumulate and the result becomes unreliable on today's noisy quantum hardware. DDRoute is a new routing algorithm that specifically minimizes circuit depth (the number of sequential steps) rather than just minimizing the total count of swaps, using a depth-driven heuristic — a rule of thumb that prioritizes shallower circuits at each decision point — to produce circuits that stay within the limits of current quantum hardware.
